moat_against: No network effects; share must be defended product-by-product against large rivals in water and coding
Mid-single-digit core growth ceiling — municipal budgets and industrial capex cycles cap demand
Product Quality & Innovation is more cyclical (consumer packaging) than Water Quality
Growth partly bought — In-Situ and GlobalVision acquisitions added 2.4pp of Q2 reported growth
Tariff and restructuring noise — Q2 2026 included a $0.05/share tariff-refund benefit and cost-optimization charges
moat_for: Razor-and-blade installed base (Hach, Trojan, ChemTreat, Videojet) driving ~62% recurring consumables/service/software revenue
Regulatory and validated-workflow switching costs in water testing and pharma/food packaging
Proven pricing power — +3% price contribution to Q2 2026 core growth
Leading brands held for decades plus Veralto Business System margin discipline
Asset-light, high-margin model — capex only $63M vs OCF $1,077M in FY2025
moat_justification: Strong moat: razor-and-blade installed base in water analytics/treatment and marking/coding drives ~62% recurring revenue, with regulatory/workflow switching costs and proven pricing power; capped below wide because growth is only mid-single-digit, there is no network effect, and capable rivals (water and coding) plus municipal/industrial cyclicality erode at the edges.
name: Veralto Corporation
one_liner: High-quality, strong-moat (7/10) compounder, but far too expensive — weighted IRR 6.97% and weighted IV@15 $35.28 vs $101.50 price; clears 15% only below ~$35.
